findings.claim: Product defect: toFahrenheit silently rounds every result to a whole degree, and the caller has no way to choose the precision or recover the exact value. By reading the code (not executed), toFahrenheit(37.5) computes exactly 99.5 and returns 100. toCelsius on line 2 does not round, so the two directions disagree: toCelsius(toFahrenheit(37.5)) gives about 37.78, not 37.5. A traveller converting a fractional forecast gets a number that differs from the true conversion, with nothing to show it was rounded. This directly contradicts V-2 and undermines the trust V-3 requires. No active obligation covers this; I-1 only uses an input whose exact result is already an integer.
findings.cause: tofahrenheit result conversion: math.round is applied unconditionally so fractional results are silently rounded with no caller-chosen precision

premises.claim: toFahrenheit wraps its whole computation in Math.round, while toCelsius returns the unrounded computation.
Neither exported function accepts a precision argument; each takes a single number.
By reading the code, toFahrenheit(100) evaluates to 212, because 100 * 9 / 5 + 32 is exactly 212 and rounding leaves it unchanged.
The architecture document describes one module, convert.ts, exporting toFahrenheit and toCelsius, which matches the code.

requests.summary: Add must-hold obligations serving V-2 and V-3, with a witness using an input whose exact result is fractional, such as toFahrenheit(37.5) = 99.5, and decide the contract for how the caller chooses precision. V-2 and V-3 are advanced by this arc, but the only active obligation, I-1, serves V-1 and uses an input whose exact result is an integer, so it cannot detect silent rounding.
